svg.aria-label: How the layers fit together in Popcorn. Down the left is a vertical Core rail (CoreDomain, Presentation, DesignSystem, CrewOrdering), the shared foundation every layer sits on. In the centre, a vertical slice: an App shell strip builds two Feature slices, MovieDetailsFeature and WatchlistFeature, which both resolve from the same Movies context below — an Application band of use cases, a Domain band with the entities and the single MovieRepository port, and an Infrastructure band with the repository implementation and the local and remote data-source ports. To the right, an Adapters box implements the Infrastructure remote port using the TMDb SDK. Beneath the slice runs a horizontal Platform strip of cross-cutting capabilities (Caching, DataPersistenceInfrastructure, FeatureAccess, Observability), each a port with its vendor SDK behind an adapter. Every dependency arrow points inward toward the Domain.
svg.text: A vertical slice, standing on shared foundations. Every arrow points inward, toward the Domain.
APP SHELL — wiring, not a layer
DOMAIN — entities + repository port · depends on nothing
PORT · the one data contract the Domain owns
use cases depend on this, never on a data source
DATA-SOURCE PORTS (defined here, not in the Domain)
PLATFORM — cross-cutting capabilities · each a port, vendor SDK behind an adapter
AppServices, the composition root, builds the TMDb-backed adapter, plugs it into the Infrastructure remote
port, assembles the Movies factory, and hands its use cases to every feature that needs movies.
The Domain, the use cases and the views never import TMDb. The arrows are the only dependencies the compiler allows.
